title: Threat Intel Feed Cache and Finding Badges Foundation
goal: Expand threat intelligence from curated records into local feed-backed context and finding badges.
scope: Add a local, approved-feed threat-intel cache and sync path for sources such as CISA KEV, ATT&CK technique data, and CVE/CVSS metadata where safely available. Finding surfaces may display KEV, ATT&CK, and source-reference badges when matched, but no external lookup may occur during assessment analysis.
generation_reason: AI_PENTESTING_AGENT.md calls for local KEV, ATT&CK, NVD/CVSS, and threat-intel context beyond the current static threat-context mapping.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Threat-intel lookups must be local at analysis time. Do not download exploits, call external APIs during scans, or claim actor attribution.

success_criteria: Approved threat-intel feeds can be synced or imported into local normalized records.
Finding surfaces can show KEV/ATT&CK/CVSS-style badges only when matched to stored local data.
Assessment-time matching does not depend on external network availability.
Sparse or stale feed data is labeled truthfully.
Tests cover sync/import, matching, stale data, and no-external-call behavior.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Threat-intel matching uses local records at analysis time.
No exploit fetching or scan-time external feed dependency is introduced.

before_promotion: Vulnerability chain detection foundation is completed and logged.
Approved feed list and stale-cache behavior are documented.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with threat-intel cache changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with local threat-intel feed and badge behavior.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.

out_of_scope: External API calls during finding analysis
